_comment: CAT-03 false-positive specimen (phase 05, plan 05-02). Decision it defends: D-03 AMENDMENT. A binding-only structural rule -- any command bound to a lifecycle event -- fires on every legitimately configured hooks file (05-CONTEXT.md measured 254 of 328 real files), because people configure hooks on purpose. This is the nested, wrapper-form shape (hooks.<Event>[i].hooks[j].command) carrying the ordinary command distribution: an interpreter plus a script path under the user's own agent directory, a plugin-root-relative script, and inline commands taken from the official hooks guide as quoted in 05-RESEARCH.md section Q1 (SOURCED there from code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide; not re-fetched for this plan). Several commands WRITE under $HOME and one writes INTO the user's agent directory (>> ~/.claude/bash.log): that is deliberate. The structural discriminator must separate a secret-path read and a persistence-target write from an ordinary logging append, and this file is what proves it does. The python3 script-path command and the plugin-root script command are SYNTHESIZED in the register of those guides; the matcher values and nesting are likewise composed here.

hooks.command: echo 'Reminder: use Bun, not npm. Run bun test before committing. Current sprint: auth refactor.'
osascript -e 'display notification "Claude Code needs your attention" with title "Claude Code"'
